jobs.title: Hedge Fund Portfolio Manager, Outsourced Chief Investment Office (OCIO) - Vice President
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States of America
jobs.description:
Position Overview:
Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing investment banking, securities, investment management, and wealth management services to a broad client base, including corporations, governments, institutions, families, and individuals. The Firm’s employees serve clients worldwide in 42 countries. As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people are critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence, and a strong team ethic. Morgan Stanley provides a superior foundation for building a professional career — a place for people to learn, achieve, and grow. A philosophy that balances personal lifestyles, perspectives, and needs is an important part of our culture.
Morgan Stanley Outsourced Chief Investment Office, or OCIO, and Morgan Stanley Family Office, or MSFO, partner with Morgan Stanley Financial Advisors across all channels to deliver portfolio management solutions to clients of Morgan Stanley Wealth Management.

Position Summary:
The Institutional Portfolio Solutions, or IPS, team is uniquely situated between two fast-growing and strategically important client channels within Morgan Stanley Wealth Management: OCIO and MSFO. These programs partner with Financial Advisors to offer discretionary and non-discretionary portfolio management services to institutional and private clients, including defined benefit plans, endowments, foundations, ultra-high-net-worth families, family offices, and other sophisticated investors.
The IPS team provides customized portfolio solutions across alternative and liquid investments and is responsible for making recommendations on portfolio construction, asset allocation, and manager selection across a broad spectrum of asset classes.

This Vice President role will focus primarily on  hedge funds and liquid alternative investments . The successful candidate must have significant experience in  both :
Sourcing, evaluating, and conducting due diligence on hedge fund managers  across multiple strategies; and Constructing customized hedge fund portfolios  for institutional, family office, ultra-high-net-worth, or other sophisticated client portfolios.
The role requires the ability to identify compelling hedge fund opportunities, evaluate managers through an institutional-quality due diligence process, and translate those views into client-specific portfolio recommendations across strategy allocation, manager selection, sizing, liquidity profile, risk management, and implementation sequencing.  This role will be client-facing and require the ability to professionally and succinctly discuss our philosophy and process, market views, portfolio updates and proposals.

Candidates with experience only in manager research or only in asset allocation / portfolio construction are unlikely to be a fit for this role. The portfolio manager / hedge fund allocator component is critical to success.

Core Responsibilities:
- Serve as a subject matter expert and portfolio manager for hedge funds and liquid alternative investments within OCIO and MSFO client portfolios.

- Source, evaluate, and conduct due diligence on hedge fund managers across strategies, including equity long/short, event-driven, credit, relative value, global macro, multi-strategy, systematic, merger arbitrage, convertible arbitrage, volatility, opportunistic, and other liquid alternative strategies.

- Maintain and expand a relevant network across the hedge fund ecosystem, including investment managers, allocators, consultants, prime brokerage contacts, capital introduction teams, and other market participants.

- Build customized hedge fund portfolios for institutional, family office, ultra-high-net-worth, and other sophisticated clients, including recommendations on strategy allocation, manager selection, position sizing, liquidity profile, implementation sequencing, and portfolio-level risk management.

- Evaluate hedge fund portfolios in the context of total client asset allocation, including public markets, private markets, liquidity needs, concentration risks, client-specific constraints, and existing portfolio exposures.

- Partner with OCIO and MSFO client segment teams and Financial Advisors to support prospective and existing client engagements, including new mandate opportunities, portfolio reviews, investment proposals, and client-specific hedge fund recommendations.

- Participate in recurring OCIO and MSFO investment meetings to discuss asset allocation, hedge fund market views, manager selection, portfolio positioning, forward pipeline opportunities, and potential portfolio changes.

- Prepare investment analyses, manager recommendations, market updates, portfolio reviews, and client-facing materials related to hedge fund and liquid alternative allocations.

- Monitor hedge fund performance, exposures, liquidity, risk characteristics, factor sensitivities, attribution, manager-specific developments, and portfolio-level contributions across OCIO and MSFO client allocations.

- Actively participate in meetings with external hedge fund managers and represent OCIO/MSFO in manager diligence, portfolio monitoring, and pipeline review discussions.

- Help drive strategic initiatives to enhance hedge fund portfolio construction, manager research, analytics, reporting, and implementation capabilities across OCIO and MSFO.

- Liaise with key internal stakeholders, partner groups, and control functions to support business initiatives, investment implementation, governance processes, and client solutions.

- Develop, enhance, or automate analytical tools, financial models, reporting processes, and data workflows to support hedge fund due diligence, portfolio construction, monitoring, and reporting.

Required Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.

- 7+ years of investment-related experience with a significant focus on hedge funds, preferably at a fund of funds, OCIO platform, institutional investment consultant, endowment, foundation, family office, alternative investment platform, or other allocator-oriented investment organization.

- Demonstrated experience sourcing hedge fund managers and maintaining a relevant network across the hedge fund manager universe.

- Demonstrated experience conducting institutional-quality hedge fund due diligence, including analysis of investment process, portfolio construction, risk management, performance attribution, liquidity, terms, operational considerations, organizational quality, and alignment of interests.

- Demonstrated experience building customized hedge fund portfolios, including manager selection, strategy allocation, position sizing, liquidity design, risk budgeting, portfolio monitoring, and rebalancing recommendations.

- Strong understanding of hedge fund strategies, including equity long/short, event-driven, credit, relative value, global macro, multi-strategy, systematic, and other liquid alternative strategies.

- Strong understanding of global capital markets, asset allocation, manager selection, modern portfolio theory, portfolio construction, performance analysis, risk management, and the broader alternative investment landscape.

- Ability to evaluate hedge fund investments at both the manager level and the total portfolio level.

- Ability to translate complex hedge fund strategy, risk, liquidity, and portfolio construction concepts into clear recommendations for sophisticated clients, Financial Advisors, investment committees, and internal stakeholders.

- Strong analytical and quantitative skills, with the ability to assess fund performance, exposures, drawdown behavior, liquidity, correlation, factor sensitivities, attribution, and portfolio-level risk.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

- High degree of professional accountability, attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and judgment.

- Proactive, hard-working, collaborative, and comfortable operating within a close-knit investment team.

Preferred Qualifications:
- CFA, CAIA, MBA, or other relevant advanced degree or professional certification.

- Experience managing or advising hedge fund-of-funds portfolios, customized hedge fund mandates, OCIO portfolios, family office hedge fund allocations, or institutional alternatives portfolios.

- Experience presenting hedge fund recommendations, portfolio construction views, and manager selection decisions to investment committees, sophisticated clients, or senior internal stakeholders.

- Experience working with portfolio analytics, exposure reporting, factor analysis, liquidity analysis, risk management tools, and performance attribution frameworks.

- Experience analyzing co-mingled hedge fund-of-funds portfolios, customized separate account portfolios, or multi-manager hedge fund programs.

- Advanced Excel skills; experience with Bloomberg, FactSet, VBA, Python, APIs, portfolio analytics platforms, or similar tools is a plus.

Technical and Analytical Skills:
The successful candidate should be comfortable working with quantitative and qualitative investment information and should be able to synthesize complex hedge fund data into actionable portfolio recommendations. Relevant technical capabilities may include:
- Performance and attribution analysis

- Exposure and factor analysis

- Liquidity and terms analysis

- Drawdown and stress scenario analysis

- Portfolio construction and optimization tools

- Manager comparison frameworks

- Excel-based modeling and reporting

- Bloomberg, FactSet, VBA, Python, APIs, or similar tools

While technical skills are important, the primary requirement for this role is demonstrated hedge fund allocator experience, including both manager sourcing/diligence and customized portfolio construction.

Licenses:
SIE, Series 7, Series 63, and Series 65, or Series 66, will be required for the role. Candidates who do not already hold these licenses will be required to obtain them after being hired within a reasonable timeframe.

ABOUT MORGAN STANLEY
Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, wealth management and investment management services. With offices in more than 41 countries, the Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments, institutions and individuals. For further information about Morgan Stanley, please visit www.morganstanley.com.

ABOUT PARAMTERIC
Parametric is part of Morgan Stanley Investment Management, the asset management division of Morgan Stanley. We partner with advisors, institutions, and consultants to build portfolios focused on what's important to them and their clients. A leader in custom solutions for more than 30 years, we help investors access efficient market exposures, solve implementation challenges, and design multi-asset portfolios that respond to their evolving needs. We also offer systematic alpha and alternative strategies to complement clients' core holdings.

This role is part of Parametric's hybrid working model, which includes working in the office 3 days a week and choosing to work remotely or in the office the remaining days of the week.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Parametric's Strategic Project Management Office (SPMO) is a varied group of Program and Project Managers at multiple levels. Our primary purpose is to drive the delivery of critical programs and projects that are structured to achieve our corporate strategy. We also serve as the central point of coordination for stakeholders, ensuring scope, timelines, blockers, and dependencies are effectively managed.

While we are focused on alignment of programs with corporate objectives and successful delivery, we place equal emphasis on individual career growth and continued improvement of SPMO capabilities. This focus on individual growth paired with continuous SPMO improvement helps ensure the team remains adaptable, high-performing, and positioned to support evolving business needs.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Principal Program Manager will be a key member of Parametric’s growing and dynamic Project Management Office. This role will work across multiple business teams and interface with technology while being chiefly responsible for structuring, planning, and executing high visibility and high priority strategic enterprise initiatives. This person will manage both programs and individual projects to drive the delivery of our corporate strategy.

As Principal Program Manager, you will play a critical role in leading large complex programs to deliver firm-wide strategic objectives by implementing business and technology solutions along with measuring the impact of these solutions. You will be responsible for overseeing and coordinating multiple projects within the program, ensuring they align with the overall strategic objectives by developing implementation plans, tracking progress and risks, clearing roadblocks, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to achieve desired business outcomes; essentially acting as a bridge between strategic planning and project execution. This role is highly cross-functional and will require a strategic thinker comfortable with ensuring cross-departmental alignment, building tools, processes, and capacity to achieve the organization’s goals. The position will report to the Director, Project Management Office but will be closely partnered with Senior Business Stakeholders and IT Leaders across the organization.

In this role, you will leverage your experience, knowledge, and skills to grow the PMO and you will be an active participant in establishing and maintaining an agile, innovative, creative, service and leadership-oriented team of project and program managers. You will be key to developing relationships across the organization and in driving toward critical business strategies and objectives. Although the Principal Program Manager will have no direct reports initially, you will be an integral part of team member development and will act as a mentor to one or more project/program managers.

ABOUT YOU
- You can affect change at Parametric.
- You are highly organized and accountable and can lead others through complex programs/projects and strategic deliveries.
- You want to be a key part in enhancing client engagement and experience while interfacing with technology delivery.
- You seek a collaborative relationship with your business partners and multiple IT delivery teams.
- You are an active learner, open-minded and innovative.
- You work well in a fast-paced constantly changing environment.
- You are interested in high-velocity software delivery with quality and customer experience in mind.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITES
- Partner with senior leaders in delivering key results to meet strategic objectives.
- Manage implementation activities for high profile, high visibility, concurrent work-streams.
- Lead program steering committee meetings to provide program updates and clear blockers.
- Develop and deliver program communications and roadmaps.
- Lead the team through translating business use cases into functional specifications and work with team leaders on work-breakdown.
- Drive issue resolution.
- Track OKRs and program success metrics.
- Bring together cross-functional business and technology teams to deliver connected, enterprise strategies, solutions, capabilities, and execution roadmaps.
- Participate in building and maintaining PMO standards, processes, and controls across the enterprise portfolio.
- Act as a mentor for other PMO resources.

JOB REQUIREMENTS
- Bachelor’s degree preferred, Master’s degree is a plus.
- 10+ years of Program Management experience required, with proven ability to manage multiple related and concurrent workstreams.
- Financial Investment Management experience is a strong plus.
- PMP, PgMP, PMI-ACP, and/or CSM certification strongly preferred.
- Proven ability as liaison between technical teams and business visionaries – not a “go between” but rather facilitator and someone who can capture the vision from both points of view into a cohesive roadmap and implementation plan.
- Lead and facilitate executive level communications, presentations, and meetings.
- Proven ability to write well-formed, clear communications and documentation.
- Excellent communication and presentation skills.
- Absolute passion for enhancing the client experience through operations and technology.

jobs.title: Fraud Link Analysis Strategy & Operations
jobs.location: Alpharetta, Georgia, United States of America
jobs.description:
In the Technology division, we leverage innovation to build the connections and capabilities that power our Firm, enabling our clients and colleagues to redefine markets and shape the future of our communities. This is a Fraud Link Analysis Strategy & Operations position at the Director level, which is part of the job family responsible for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks to ensure operational continuity and resilience in the face of potential threats or disruptions that could impact the organization, plus management of ongoing incidents.

Morgan Stanley is an industry leader in financial services, known for mobilizing capital to help governments, corporations, institutions, and individuals around the world achieve their financial goals.

Interested in joining a team that’s eager to create, innovate and make an impact on the world? Read on.

This Director position will lead the operational execution and strategic development of fraud link analysis capabilities that leverage graph analytics and investigative tooling to identify, investigate, and mitigate complex fraud patterns. This role serves as a bridge between Fraud Operations, Fraud Technology, Analytics, and investigative teams by translating operational fraud needs into technical requirements, validating tool outputs, and ensuring graph-based insights are actionable for fraud review and remediation.

What you'll do in the role:
- Graph Analytics Tool Partnership: Collaborate with technology, data strategists, analytics, and linking operations teams to define requirements, prioritize enhancements, and support development of graph analytics tools used to detect and investigate fraud linkages.

- Data Integration and Readiness: Provide fraud operations subject matter expertise to guide the integration of account, party, transaction, device, payee, employee, known fraud, and other relevant data into graphing tools and investigative platforms.

- Output Testing and Validation: Test graph analytics outputs, validate query logic and business rules, assess data quality, identify false positives or gaps, and provide feedback to technology partners to improve tool accuracy and usability.

- Operational Strategy Development: Develop practical review strategies, workflow guidance, escalation thresholds, and handoff processes that enable operations teams to consistently review graph outputs and convert insights into fraud mitigation actions.

- Fraud Alert and Case Review: Perform hands-on review of potentially fraudulent activity based on graphing tool outputs. Based on review, document findings and recommend account-level or event-level actions.

- Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner with fraud investigations, alerting, event management, controls, analytics, technology, and leadership teams to align graph analytics capabilities with fraud typologies, operational needs, and risk reduction priorities.

- Procedure and Governance Support: Create and maintain operating procedures, review standards, quality control expectations, metrics, and documentation supporting the use of graph analytics in fraud operations.

- Emerging Fraud Response: Support the identification, investigation, escalation, and mitigation of emerging fraud events by using graph analytics to identify connected accounts, parties, counterparties, devices, or behavioral patterns.

What you'll bring to the role:
- 5–8 years of experience in fraud risk, financial crimes, or a related investigative or operational role at a global financial institution

- Familiarity with Agile methodologies, as well as project management tools including JIRA

- Expertise with fraud case management, alerting systems, known fraud databases, or fraud analytics platforms

- Knowledge with onboarding tooling related to fraud case management, alerting systems, known fraud databases, or fraud analytics platforms

- Experience with the development of fraud strategies, enabling technology or managing large scale projects

- Experience working with technologists, documenting requirements and explaining business requirements

- BA or BS preferred, but not required

Preferred Experience
- Experience with graph database or graph visualization platforms such as Neo4j, Bloom, NeoDash, or similar tools.

- Knowledge of digital asset transactions (i.e. crypto)

- Familiarity with creation of AI agents and using AI technologies to create operational and strategic efficiencies

- Knowledge on SQL or Python for data analytics

Wealth Management Operations
Wealth Management (WM) Operations is a global organization operating in 21 cities across 4 countries in support of the Wealth Management business.  The organization drives operational excellence by supporting business growth, enhancing the client experience, and improving operational efficiency with a strong foundation in risk and financial management.

Capital Markets, Core Processing and Risk  supports the movement of client assets in and out of the Firm, provide asset servicing for our clients, and offer front-to-back support to clients throughout the lifecycle of a trade.  CMCPR’s primary focus is to provide first class service to our business partners, financial advisors and clients while mitigating financial, reputation, and regulatory risk to the Firm.

Overview of role:
We are seeking a Vice President to join Morgan Stanley’s Wealth Management Operations Capital Markets, Core Processing & Risk (CMCPR) organization’s COO team as the Transformation, Metrics & Analytics lead.  They will be responsible for shaping and driving the department’s transformation and automation agenda, operating model, governance framework, transformation and automation strategy and portfolio.  The successful candidate will partner closely with Operations leadership, Technology, Finance, Risk, and Global Operations Transformation teams to drive strategic initiatives that improve scalability, operational effectiveness, risk management, and organizational performance.
This individual will provide leadership and oversight across the department’s transformation and automation portfolio, ensuring alignment with Firmwide and Operations’ priorities while establishing the governance, metrics, and management disciplines necessary to sustain long-term transformation.  The role requires an experienced individual with the ability to translate strategy into execution, drive organizational alignment, and influence senior stakeholders across a complex, matrixed environment.
The ideal candidate combines strong business acumen with a deep understanding of operating model design, process optimization, performance management, automation, artificial intelligence, and organizational transformation.  They will play a critical role in modernizing how CMCPR operates while enabling the department to deliver against evolving business, client, regulatory, and operational priorities.

Transformation Strategy & Execution
- Lead the development and execution of the CMCPR transformation strategy, ensuring alignment with departmental objectives, WM Operations priorities, and the Global Operations Transformation goals and agenda.

- Oversight of the department’s transformation portfolio, including strategic initiatives, automation programs, operating model enhancements, and productivity initiatives.

- Identify opportunities to improve organizational effectiveness, operational scalability, risk management, and capacity creation through process redesign, workflow optimization, and technology enablement.

- Drive adoption of emerging technologies, including workflow automation, artificial intelligence (GenAI, Agentic AI), software solutions, and intelligent document processing capabilities.

- Oversee the CMCPR automation strategy and centralized automation function, including governance, prioritization, resource allocation, and delivery oversight.

- Champion a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, transformational mindset, and operational excellence (reimagining operations) across the organization.

- Drive adoption of automation capabilities and self-service tools across the department, promoting scalable solutions and reusability across functions.

- Partner with Operations and Technology teams to accelerate modernization efforts and maximize business value realization.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management
- Serve as a trusted advisor to CMCPR leadership on transformation, operating model, governance, performance management, and organizational priorities.

- Build strong partnerships across Operations, Technology, Risk, Finance, Control Functions, and Global Transformation teams.

- Influence senior stakeholders and drive alignment across competing priorities through data-driven recommendations and strategic leadership.

- Lead and develop the department’s Transformation, Metrics & Analytics team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous development.

Required Qualifications:
- 10+ years of relevant experience in Operations, Business Management, COO, Transformation, Strategy, Consulting, Program Management, or related disciplines.

- 3+ years of people leadership experience, with a demonstrated track record of building, developing, and leading high-performing teams in a complex, matrixed environment.

- Demonstrated leadership experience driving large-scale transformation initiatives within complex financial services organizations.

- Strong understanding of operating model design, governance frameworks, organizational effectiveness, and execution management.

- Experience establishing and managing transformation portfolios, executive governance structures, and performance management disciplines.

- Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and lead cross-functional initiatives in a matrixed environment.

jobs.description:
We’re seeking a Strategy Metrics & KPI Lead (Vice President) to shape how Morgan Stanley measures progress and outcomes across the firm's technology strategy. As part of the Enterprise Architecture and Modernization (EAM) Metrics & KPIs function, this role leads the firm's technology measurement ecosystem, partnering across architecture, engineering, cybersecurity, data, infrastructure, and senior leadership to define trusted, standardized metrics that inform decision-making across Technology Strategy priorities.

The role combines technology strategy, data architecture, analytics, KPI governance, and hands-on implementation, leveraging AI technologies where appropriate. It will measure outcomes across modernization, governance, resilience, engineering excellence, platform adoption, data readiness, productivity, operational efficiency, and other strategic priorities. Measures may include AI adoption and productivity as part of a much broader technology strategy measurement mandate.

The successful candidate will establish the measurement foundations that help leaders assess outcomes, quantify value, and identify areas requiring action. This includes identifying key datasets, improving data quality, defining common metrics, and enabling broad consumption of strategy insights through executive dashboards, self-service analytics, and reporting platforms.

The EAM team drives firmwide technology strategy through scalable, resilient architectures, governance, and standards. By advancing cloud, data, distributed systems, and AI capabilities, they accelerate modernization, optimize technology investments, and foster a global architecture community focused on innovation and long-term value.

In the Technology division, we leverage innovation to build the connections and capabilities that power our Firm, enabling our clients and colleagues to redefine markets and shape
the future of our communities. This is a Lead Data & Analytics Engineering position at Vice President level, which is part of the job family responsible for providing specialist data analysis and expertise that drive decision-making and business insights as well as crafting data pipelines, implementing data models, and optimizing data processes for improved data accuracy and accessibility, including applying machine learning and AI-based techniques.

Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, always evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.

What you’ll do in the role:
- Partner with stakeholders across every division to define, standardize, and govern the metrics and KPIs tracking progress against the firm's strategic technology priorities, building on the ongoing refresh of the technology strategy scorecard now underway across engineering, data, architecture, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and business teams.

- Develop leading and lagging indicators that give leadership visibility into adoption, enablement, modernization, simplification, technology health, resilience, governance maturity, productivity gains, operational efficiency, platform convergence, and measurable business value.

- Establish consistent measurement approaches across the major pillars of the technology strategy, including business and corporate enablement, technology modernization and simplification, governance and operating model maturity, resilience and risk reduction, engineering excellence, platform adoption, data readiness, and selective AI-related measures where they contribute to broader strategy outcomes.

- Produce strategic insights, trend analyses, dashboards, and executive reporting that help leaders evaluate transformation impact and guide future investment, continuing the buildout of self-service analytics environments maturing from static reporting into interactive, model-driven exploration.

- Design and deliver the technical architecture that aggregates, publishes, and enables querying of enterprise strategy datasets, including reconciliation, normalization, stewardship, lifecycle management, and repeatable publication of underlying metrics.

- Define semantic models, metadata standards, business glossaries, lineage requirements, and data quality controls so that technology strategy metrics are consistently understood, discoverable, trusted, and reusable across the firm.

- Partner with data, engineering, architecture, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and divisional technology teams to source and validate metrics from systems of record, program inventories, operating dashboards, and other trusted enterprise data sources.

- Incorporate resilience, technology-health, risk, control, and readiness indicators into the broader strategy narrative so leadership has one coherent view of progress, gaps, and execution risk across the technology estate.

- Serve as a trusted partner to senior stakeholders, facilitating alignment across groups with differing priorities, and play a central role in curating proposed strategy metrics as they move from draft concepts toward finalized, adopted reporting measures.

What you’ll bring to the role:
- 10+ years of experience in data engineering, data architecture, analytics, KPI development, technology strategy, or technology governance, with a track record of engaging senior stakeholders across large, complex organizations.

- Experience defining, implementing, and governing enterprise-scale metrics and performance measurement frameworks, including scorecards, executive KPI dashboards, strategic measurement frameworks, and multi-source reporting environments.

- Demonstrated ability to transform fragmented technology data into trusted, actionable insights that support decision making, investment prioritization, and strategy execution.

- Background in data engineering and data architecture, including hands-on experience designing pipelines, dimensional and canonical data models, reconciliation logic, curated data products, and reusable analytical datasets on enterprise platforms such as Snowflake, Databricks, Dataiku, or similar technologies.

- Knowledge of data modeling, semantic modeling, metadata management, data governance, and data quality practices, applying techniques such as profiling, validation rule design, lineage mapping, metric definition, business glossary development, and reference data standardization.

- SQL and Python skills for data analysis, validation, prototyping, and exploration; data analyst experience with dashboards and analytics platforms such as Power BI or Tableau is preferred but not required.

- Understanding technology modernization, enterprise platforms, software engineering, cloud technologies, architecture governance, operational resilience, technology risk, and emerging technology capabilities, including AI where relevant to technology strategy measurement.

- Communication and stakeholder management skills, applying facilitation and prioritization techniques to influence without direct authority across organizational boundaries and balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

- Analytical and problem-solving capabilities, using structured, root-cause-driven approaches to diagnose measurement gaps while operating in highly collaborative environments spanning architecture, engineering, cybersecurity, infrastructure, data, and business stakeholders.

Responsable des indicateurs de performance (Metrics & KPI) de la stratégie technologique (hybride)Nous sommes à la recherche d'un(e) responsable des Strategy Metrics & KPI (vice-présidence) afin de définir la façon dont Morgan Stanley mesure les progrès et les résultats de sa stratégie technologique. Au sein de la fonction Metrics & KPIs d’Enterprise Architecture and Modernization (EAM), cette personne dirigera l’écosystème de mesure technologique de l’entreprise et collaborera avec les équipes d’architecture, d’ingénierie, de cybersécurité, de données, d’infrastructure ainsi qu’avec la haute direction afin de définir des mesures fiables et normalisées qui soutiennent la prise de décision relativement aux priorités de la Technology Strategy.

Ce rôle combine la stratégie technologique, l’architecture des données, l’analytique, la gouvernance des KPI et la mise en œuvre pratique, tout en tirant parti des technologies d’IA lorsque cela est approprié. Il permettra de mesurer les résultats liés à la modernisation, à la gouvernance, à la résilience, à l’excellence en ingénierie, à l’adoption des plateformes, à la préparation des données, à la productivité, à l’efficacité opérationnelle ainsi qu’à d’autres priorités stratégiques. Les mesures pourront notamment inclure l’adoption de l’IA et les gains de productivité, dans le cadre d’un mandat beaucoup plus vaste de mesure de la stratégie technologique.

La personne retenue établira les fondements de mesure permettant aux dirigeants d’évaluer les résultats, de quantifier la valeur créée et de déterminer les domaines nécessitant des actions. Cela comprend l’identification des jeux de données clés, l’amélioration de la qualité des données, la définition de mesures communes ainsi que la diffusion à grande échelle d’informations stratégiques au moyen de tableaux de bord destinés à la direction, d’outils de self-service analytics et de plateformes de production de rapports.

L’équipe EAM met en œuvre la stratégie technologique de l’entreprise à l’échelle mondiale grâce à des architectures évolutives et résilientes, ainsi qu’à des cadres de gouvernance et des normes établies. En faisant progresser les capacités liées au cloud, aux données, aux systèmes distribués et à l’IA, elle accélère la modernisation, optimise les investissements technologiques et favorise une communauté mondiale d’architecture axée sur l’innovation et la création de valeur à long terme.

Dans la division Technologie, nous misons sur l’innovation pour développer les connexions et les capacités qui propulsent notre Société, permettant à notre clientèle et à nos collègues de redéfinir les marchés et de façonner l’avenir de nos collectivités. Ce poste de direction en ingénierie des données et de l’analytique, de niveau vice-présidence, fait partie de la famille d’emplois responsable de fournir une expertise spécialisée en analyse des données afin d’orienter la prise de décision et de générer des renseignements d’affaires pertinents. Le rôle consiste également à concevoir des pipelines de données, à mettre en œuvre des modèles de données et à optimiser les processus de gestion des données afin d’améliorer l’exactitude et l’accessibilité des données, notamment par l’application de techniques d’apprentissage automatique (machine learning) et d’intelligence artificielle (IA).

Depuis 1935, Morgan Stanley est reconnu comme un chef de file mondial des services financiers, évoluant et innovant constamment afin de mieux servir sa clientèle et les collectivités où elle exerce ses activités dans plus de 40 pays à travers le monde.

Ce que vous ferez dans ce rôle :
Collaborer avec les parties prenantes de chaque division afin de définir, normaliser et encadrer les métriques et les KPI servant à mesurer les progrès réalisés par rapport aux priorités stratégiques technologiques de l'entreprise, en s'appuyant sur la mise à jour en cours du tableau de bord de la stratégie technologique à travers les équipes d'engineering, de data, d'architecture, d'infrastructure, de cybersécurité et d'affaires.
Développer des indicateurs avancés et retardés permettant à la direction d'avoir une visibilité sur l'adoption, l'habilitation, la modernisation, la simplification, la santé technologique, la résilience, la maturité de la gouvernance, les gains de productivité, l'efficacité opérationnelle, la convergence des plateformes et la valeur d'affaires mesurable.
Établir des approches de mesure cohérentes pour les principaux axes de la stratégie technologique, notamment l'habilitation des secteurs d'affaires et des fonctions corporatives, la modernisation et la simplification technologique, la maturité de la gouvernance et du modèle opérationnel, la résilience et la réduction des risques, l'excellence en engineering, l'adoption des plateformes, la préparation des données (data readiness) et certaines mesures liées à l'AI lorsque celles-ci contribuent aux résultats stratégiques globaux.
Produire des analyses stratégiques, des analyses de tendances, des tableaux de bord et des rapports destinés à la haute direction afin d'évaluer l'impact des transformations et d'orienter les investissements futurs, tout en poursuivant l'évolution des environnements d'analytique en libre-service (self-service analytics) d'un modèle de rapports statiques vers des capacités d'exploration interactives basées sur des modèles.
Concevoir et mettre en œuvre l'architecture technique permettant d'agréger, de publier et de rendre interrogeables les ensembles de données stratégiques de l'entreprise, y compris le rapprochement des données, la normalisation, la gestion responsable des données (data stewardship), la gestion du cycle de vie et la publication répétable des métriques sous-jacentes.
Définir les modèles sémantiques (semantic models), les normes de métadonnées, les glossaires d'affaires, les exigences de traçabilité (data lineage) et les contrôles de qualité des données afin que les métriques liées à la stratégie technologique soient comprises de façon uniforme, faciles à repérer, fiables et réutilisables à travers l'entreprise.
Collaborer avec les équipes de data, d'engineering, d'architecture, de cybersécurité, d'infrastructure et de technologie des différentes divisions afin d'obtenir et de valider les métriques provenant des systèmes de référence (systems of record), des inventaires de programmes, des tableaux de bord opérationnels et d'autres sources de données d'entreprise fiables.
Intégrer les indicateurs de résilience, de santé technologique, de risque, de contrôle et de préparation dans le récit stratégique global afin de fournir à la direction une vision cohérente des progrès, des écarts et des risques d'exécution à travers l'ensemble de l'environnement technologique de l'entreprise.
Agir à titre de partenaire de confiance auprès des parties prenantes principales, favoriser l'alignement entre des groupes ayant des priorités différentes et jouer un rôle central dans l'évaluation et l'évolution des métriques stratégiques proposées, depuis leur élaboration initiale jusqu'à leur adoption comme mesures officielles de reddition de comptes.

Ce que vous apporterez à ce rôle :
Plus de 10 ans d'expérience en data engineering, architecture de données (data architecture), analytique, développement de KPI, stratégie technologique ou gouvernance technologique, avec une expérience démontrée de collaboration auprès de parties prenantes de niveau supérieur au sein d'organisations complexes et d'envergure.
Expérience dans la définition, la mise en œuvre et la gouvernance de métriques et de cadres de mesure de la performance à l'échelle de l'entreprise, notamment des tableaux de bord stratégiques (scorecards), des tableaux de bord exécutifs de KPI, des cadres de mesure stratégique et des environnements de production de rapports multisources.
Capacité démontrée à transformer des données technologiques fragmentées en informations fiables et exploitables soutenant la prise de décision, la priorisation des investissements et l'exécution de la stratégie.
Expérience en data engineering et en architecture de données, incluant une expérience pratique dans la conception de pipelines de données, de modèles dimensionnels et canoniques, de logiques de rapprochement, de produits de données organisés (curated data products) et d'ensembles de données analytiques réutilisables sur des plateformes d'entreprise telles que Snowflake, Databricks, Dataiku ou des technologies similaires.
Connaissance de la modélisation des données, de la modélisation sémantique (semantic modeling), de la gestion des métadonnées, de la gouvernance des données et des pratiques de qualité des données, notamment l'utilisation de techniques telles que le profilage des données, la conception de règles de validation, la cartographie de la traçabilité (lineage mapping), la définition de métriques, l'élaboration de glossaires d'affaires et la normalisation des données de référence.
Maîtrise de SQL et Python pour l'analyse, la validation, le prototypage et l'exploration des données. Une expérience comme analyste de données avec des tableaux de bord et des plateformes analytiques telles que Power BI ou Tableau constitue un atout, sans être obligatoire.
Bonne compréhension de la modernisation technologique, des plateformes d'entreprise, du génie logiciel, des technologies infonuagiques (cloud technologies), de la gouvernance de l'architecture, de la résilience opérationnelle, des risques technologiques et des capacités technologiques émergentes, y compris l'AI lorsqu'elle est pertinente aux mesures de la stratégie technologique.
Excellentes compétences en communication et en gestion des parties prenantes, avec la capacité d'utiliser des techniques de facilitation et de priorisation pour exercer une influence sans autorité directe à travers les unités organisationnelles, tout en conciliant réflexion stratégique et exécution concrète.

jobs.description:
Corporate FP&A is seeking a curious, motivated Analyst / Associate to support firmwide budgeting, forecasting, controls and strategic transformation initiatives, including our Strategic Transformation work on Integrated Forecasting. In this role, you'll help translate data into clear insights for senior stakeholders, build dashboards and presentation materials, and partner across Finance to deliver outputs that are accurate, well-documented and on time. We're especially interested in candidates who bring a technology/optimization mindset-someone who looks for opportunities to automate, standardize and continuously improve how we work.

In the Finance division, we act as a partner to business units around the globe by providing management, review, analysis and advisory services of the Firm's financial and capital resources. This is a Analyst/Associate position within our Risk, Assurance, Governance & Control Job Family which provides oversight and monitoring of operational risk or third party/outsourcing for the global Finance division, validation and testing of financial and regulatory reports and reinforcement of regulatory requirements, policies and procedures

Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, always evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.

What you'll do in the role:

- Continuously assess and develop business processes with the objective of enhancing advisory calibre and implementation efficiency

- Subject Matter Expertise : You bring strong knowledge of employer-sponsored health benefits, including medical, dental, vision, and pharmacy, along with broader healthcare industry experience across vendors, payers, and health systems.

- Analytical Mindset: You use data to guide decisions and identify ways to strengthen strategy, administration, and outcomes.
- Flexibility & Accountability: You work well in a fast-paced environment, adapt quickly to change, and deliver accurate, timely results.
- Collaboration: You partner effectively across teams and leadership, incorporate diverse perspectives, and help develop plans aligned to organizational goals.

- Analyze current benefit plans and programs to assess competitiveness, determine gaps and identify opportunities
- Benchmark our plans, products and vendors against our peers continuously; use market data to help identify trends to inform benefits and well-being strategies
- Monitor health plan performance, utilization patterns and cost trends to inform plan changes that improve financial management and plan  efficiency, in conjunction with Benefits Analytics
- Assess qualitative and quantitative implications of benefit plan changes; develop business cases for proposed changes, including pricing considerations
- Collaborate on a multi-year strategy for our health plans and vendors that focuses on health outcomes, quality, cost and the employee experience
- Stay up-to-date on industry trends and vendor offering developments

- Lead or assist with vendor RFPs and vendor selection process
- Work in close partnership with team lead to develop strategy around new vendor design and implementation, including program configuration, pricing structure, and communications, in conjunction with internal Benefits, Sourcing, Legal, Technology and Communications partners

General plan management and governance
- Conduct annual vendor contracts review and negotiations with a focus on performance guarantees
- Collaborate on annual review and updating of SPDs
- Support Annual Enrollment processes
- Stay current on regulatory and legislative developments; partner with ERISA counsel and vendors to assess impact and implement required plan and document updates.

- Analyze plan data to inform benefit strategy using data warehouse
- Support data gathering and analysis for external surveys on our benefit offerings

Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing (“MSREI”) is the global private real estate investment management business of Morgan Stanley. One of the most active property investors in the world for over three decades, MSREI employs a patient, disciplined approach through global value-add / opportunistic and regional core / core-plus real estate investment strategies.

With 17 offices throughout the U.S., Europe and Asia, regional teams of dedicated real estate professionals combine a unique global perspective with local presence and significant transaction execution expertise. MSREI currently manages $58 billion of gross real estate assets worldwide on behalf of its clients.

MSREI is seeking a highly experienced Executive Director of Asset Management to oversee a significant portion of MSREI’s industrial portfolio across its various fund strategies. The Executive Director will assume responsibility for a strategically important, multi-market industrial portfolio of approximately $3 billion in Gross Asset Value (GAV); comprising roughly 70 assets totaling over 14.5 million square feet and approximately 130 tenancies across six major U.S. markets. This role represents one of the business’s largest dedicated industrial asset management positions.

A successful candidate will optimize portfolio performance by leveraging direct tenant relationships to drive leasing and retention, actively managing brokers to deliver leasing goals, and holding property management accountable for quality of operations. The role demands a highly organized, execution-oriented asset manager with substantial hands-on experience managing industrial assets. The ideal candidate is experienced working through the complex challenges that arise across a portfolio of this scale, overseeing capital improvement projects and repairs, and building and managing tenant relationships. Above all, this individual will drive accountability across internal and external stakeholders while maintaining a relentless focus on leasing performance and value creation.

- Develop and execute asset-level business plans focused on maximizing value and operating performance.
- Drive portfolio performance through leasing execution, tenant retention, capital planning, and revenue optimization.
- Monitor asset performance against underwriting and investment objectives.
- Lead leasing strategy across approximately 3.5 million square feet of near-term roll.
- Coordinate closely with leasing brokers to establish market strategy, pricing, marketing, and transaction execution.
- Negotiate lease agreements with tenants.
- Manage property managers, leasing professionals, construction managers, and third-party service providers to ensure execution of business plans.
- Coordinate capital projects and repositioning initiatives where appropriate.
- Prepare and present investment recommendations and leasing approvals.
- Lead quarterly asset reviews and annual business planning.
- Monitor market fundamentals, competitive positioning, tenant demand, and valuation trends.
- Identify opportunities to enhance portfolio value through leasing, redevelopment, or disposition.

- 10+ years of commercial real estate experience with significant industrial asset management responsibility.
- Proven experience leading leasing strategy for large industrial portfolios.
- Strong understanding of industrial market dynamics across multiple U.S. regions.
- Experience managing third-party property managers and leasing brokers.
- Excellent financial analysis, valuation, and investment decision-making skills.
- Ability to prioritize competing initiatives across numerous assets simultaneously.
- Strong communication and organizational leadership capabilities.

Excellent opportunity for recent or soon to be 2027 graduates! Office Locations: Seattle, Boston, Minneapolis, Alpharetta

SUMMER COHORT STARTS - July 2027

ABOUT THE OPERATIONS ANALYST PROGRAM

The Operations Analyst Program is an early-career development opportunity for driven recent and soon-to-be graduates who want to launch a career at the intersection of investment management, operations, data, and technology. Analysts use analytical, technical, and collaborative skills to help deliver operational excellence, solve business challenges, and improve outcomes for clients.
As investment operations evolve through data, automation, and AI, analysts gain hands-on experience supporting business-critical investment processes while helping identify opportunities to improve how work gets done. Through ownership of operational processes and exposure to continuous improvement, data analytics, automation, workflow design, and AI, analysts strengthen controls, improve decision-making, and contribute to scalable solutions that support clients and business growth.
Over three weeks, Analysts begin as a cohort with an immersion in Parametric's investment strategies, operating model, and Operations organization. Following onboarding, analysts join teams supporting Market, Client, or Control functions, where they develop domain expertise, learn business-critical workflows, and build an end-to-end understanding of how Operations supports clients, portfolios, risk management, and business growth.
Operations teams are responsible for the execution, oversight, servicing, and control activities that support the investment lifecycle. Analysts work closely with teammates and stakeholders across the organization to execute processes accurately, resolve operational challenges, improve controls, and deliver exceptional client outcomes.
In addition to their core team responsibilities, analysts may collaborate with specialized teams within Operations focused on process transformation, analytics, workflow modernization, automation, and AI-enabled solutions. Partnering with subject matter experts across Market, Client, and Control functions to identify opportunities, redesign processes, and implement scalable improvements that enhance operational effectiveness. Through this partnership, analysts may gain exposure to transformation initiatives while continuing to build deep operational expertise.
The program is designed for people who are curious about how businesses operate, motivated to improve processes, and eager to continue learning. As business needs evolve, analysts may gain exposure to different Operations functions, participate in cross-functional initiatives, or contribute to transformation efforts, broadening their knowledge, experience, and skill sets.

WHAT YOU'LL DO AND LEARN
- Learn Parametric's investment strategies, operating model, and business-critical Operations workflows, and understand how Market, Client, and Control functions support clients, portfolios, risk management, and business growth.

- Learn and execute business-critical investment operations workflows accurately and on time. Responsibilities may include activities such as cash and position reconciliation, trade lifecycle support, client servicing, corporate actions, account onboarding and maintenance, contracts, oversight activities, and billing, depending on team assignment.

- Develop an end-to-end understanding of assigned processes, including activities, decisions, systems, data flows, controls, handoffs, and upstream and downstream dependencies.

- Investigate exceptions, breaks, recurring operational issues, and client-impacting events using structured problem-solving and data analysis. Identify root causes, assess impacts, and recommend sustainable solutions.

- Partner with Operations teams, portfolio managers, traders, sales, product management, technology teams, external providers, and other stakeholders to resolve issues, improve handoffs, and support business priorities.

- Perform quality control and verification activities, maintain accurate records and documentation, and help ensure operational processes meet established policies, procedures, and control standards.

- Analyze operational and investment data to identify patterns, anomalies, trends, bottlenecks, and emerging risks. Build reports, dashboards, or analytical tools that turn data into actionable insights and improvement opportunities.

- Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, or redesign workflows and contribute to process mapping, requirements gathering, testing, implementation, and adoption activities.

- Collaborate with Automation, Reinvention & Collaboration (ARC) and other partners on process-improvement initiatives, workflow modernization efforts, analytics projects, automation solutions, and AI-enabled capabilities.

- Associate or bachelor's degree completed by the program start date. Relevant fields may include industrial, process, or systems engineering; operations research; supply chain; data science or analytics; computer science; information systems; mathematics; statistics; finance; accounting; economics; or a related analytical, business, or technical field. Candidates from other majors with relevant quantitative, technical, or process-improvement experience are also encouraged to apply.

jobs.location: New York, New York, United States of America
jobs.description:
Morgan Stanley Investment Management (MSIM) is one of the largest global asset management organizations of any full-service securities firm, with more than 50 years of history, a presence in 26 countries, and a total of $1.9 trillion in assets under management as of March 31, 2026.

MSIM provides broad-based specialization across a range of asset classes in public and private markets. Our independent investment teams leverage Morgan Stanley’s global resources to serve a diverse client base of governments, institutions, corporations, advisors and individuals worldwide. Our investment solutions include a broad range of alternatives, high-conviction active strategies, customization strategies, ESG expertise and tax management solutions.  For further information about Morgan Stanley Investment Management, please visit   www.morganstanley.com/im

The Hedge Fund Solutions team constructs and manages hedge fund strategies, portfolios, and solutions on behalf of institutional and high net-worth clients through its various pooled vehicles (limited partnerships) and segregated accounts. Riverview Omni Fund LP (“Omni”) is a market and factor neutral multi-manager equity hedge fund within Hedge Fund Solutions. Launched in July 2021, Omni oversees approximately $2B AUM as of October 2026. Omni allocates capital to portfolio managers who run fundamental equity relative value and quantitative investment strategies.

Omni is a multi-manager hedge fund platform, overseeing a portfolio of high-quality trading teams, specializing in long/short fundamental equities, quantitative, and non-correlated (“orthogonal”) trading strategies. The Fund, by design, is a market and factor managed platform covering of all the major GIC industries, quantitative equity and futures trading strategies (diversified across time horizons) and independent, relative value strategies with well-behaved distributional properties. The Fund’s primary investment objective is to provide investors consistent and attractive risk-adjusted returns with low correlation to global capital markets by investing in a variety of investment strategies and employing principles that seek to maximize active risk, minimize inter-manager correlations and manage overall volatility levels.

The Fund management team seeks to achieve this investment objective by engaging and overseeing multiple investment managers and their respective portfolios, each of which is expected to operate within pre-existing investment and risk guidelines, employing one of the three broad strategies. The team allocates capital using a modified equal risk contribution methodology, targets total Fund volatility levels through the efficient gross deployment of capital, and manages unwanted market and factor exposures using an internally managed central trading layer portfolio.

The Senior Equity Risk Manager will be joining the Central Trading and Risk Management team of a multi-manager, market-neutral equity hedge fund. This team partners directly with portfolio managers to optimize portfolio construction, manage risk, develop quantitative investment tools, and improve investment performance across the platform. This is a highly analytical and market-oriented role at the intersection of risk management, portfolio construction, quantitative research, and investing.

As a senior member of the team, this individual will work closely with the Chief Investment Officer, Chief Risk Officer, Business Development team, and individual Portfolio Managers across the platform, while also playing a significant role in managing and developing the fund’s central trading and risk management infrastructure. The Senior Equity Risk Manager thinks like an investor and portfolio manager, while bringing the analytical discipline and independence required of a senior risk professional. The successful candidate is intellectually curious, collaborative, and enjoys solving complex investment problems using data and quantitative methods. They are equally comfortable discussing a portfolio's factor and concentration risks with a fundamental PM, building an empirical framework to test a portfolio-construction hypothesis, evaluating a new systematic alpha signal, and working through the optimization and execution details required to put that signal into production.

Responsibilities

- Work directly with PMs to identify and manage portfolio risks, including factor, industry, thematic, concentration, liquidity, crowding, correlation, event, and other sources of systematic and idiosyncratic exposure.

- Advise PMs on portfolio construction, position sizing, hedging, diversification, and factor management, with the objective of improving portfolio robustness and risk-adjusted returns.

- Analyze portfolio behavior across different market environments and stress scenarios, distinguishing intended investment exposures from unintended or inefficient risks.

- Evaluate portfolio performance and sources of alpha, including attribution across factors, sectors, themes, and individual positions; identify persistent strengths, weaknesses, and opportunities to improve portfolio construction.

- Contribute to platform-level decisions regarding risk allocation, capital deployment, portfolio constraints, and the interaction of individual PM portfolios within the overall fund.

- Research, develop, and evaluate alpha signals using market, fundamental, alternative, positioning, and other relevant datasets.

- Develop and enhance portfolio construction and optimization methodologies, including alpha combination, risk-model integration, exposure management, turnover and transaction-cost controls, and portfolio constraints.

- Monitor market developments and proactively communicate portfolio risks, opportunities, and positioning implications to portfolio managers and senior leadership.

- Partner with trading to improve execution and implementation efficiency.

- Design and develop Python-based analytical tools, research infrastructure, and automation that improve portfolio analytics and investment workflows.

Requirements

- A minimum of 8-10 years of relevant professional experience in equity risk management, quantitative investing/research, systematic investing, portfolio management, trading, or fundamental or quantitative equity investing. Prior experience in a role involving direct investment or trading decisions is strongly preferred.

- Deep understanding of equity markets and portfolio risk, ideally developed through direct experience working with or managing market-neutral, factor-constrained equity portfolios.

- Strong knowledge of portfolio construction and optimization, factor models, risk decomposition, position sizing, hedging, portfolio constraints, and market impact modeling.

- Strong quantitative and statistical skills, with the ability to conduct rigorous empirical research and translate the results into practical investment decisions.

- Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience working with large financial datasets and developing production-quality analytical or research tools.

- Experience with systematic alpha research, portfolio optimization, execution research, or quantitative equity strategies is highly desirable.

- Prior experience in investing, trading, quantitative research, or another role involving direct responsibility for investment decisions and outcomes is strongly preferred.

- Strong intuition for how portfolios behave in real markets—not simply how they appear within a risk model—including liquidity, positioning, crowding, catalysts, market microstructure, and changing correlations.

- Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain sophisticated quantitative and risk concepts clearly to Portfolio Managers and senior investment professionals.

- Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving investment environment, independently identify important problems, and move comfortably between detailed quantitative research and higher-level portfolio judgment.

Who you are

- Operates with a strong sense of ethics and integrity in your interactions with others and decision making.

- Takes accountability and ownership in your work with a focus on long-term value creation.

- Track record of fostering a culture of honesty, transparency and accountability within teams.

- Proven ability to collaborate across teams to deliver optimal solutions for clients.

- A passion for innovation, with a continuous improvement mindset to drive excellence.

- Respect for individual differences, with an openness to diverse perspectives.

- Engagement in community service, volunteering or corporate citizenship initiatives.

- Commitment to mentoring and supporting professional growth of others.

Background on the Position
The role will focus on Third Party and Business Disruption & Resilience (BDR) operational risk management and resides within Legal and Compliance's Non-Financial Risk (NFR) department, a Second Line of Defense (2LoD) function. Operational risk refers to the risk of financial or other loss, or potential damage to a firm's reputation, resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, or systems or from external events. The Firm may incur operational risk across the full scope of its business activities, including revenue-generating activities (e.g., sales and trading) and control groups (e.g., information technology and trade processing).

The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting independent oversight, analysis, and challenge of Third Party and BDR risks and controls. The individual will play a key role in executing risk management oversight activities, including execution of risk assessments and regulatory compliance monitoring, creation of governance materials, and review of incidents and issues, remediation activity, and other matters requiring independent review and challenge.

Primary Responsibilities
> Execute Second Line non-financial risk oversight activities to support oversight and challenge of Third Party and BDR risk.
> Support independent review and challenge through execution of risk assessments as well as review of control outcomes, issues, incidents, remediation plans, and risk acceptances related to Third Party specialized risks.
> Assist with governance activities related to Third Party specialized risks, including preparation and review of materials, meeting documentation, action tracking, and escalation summaries.
> Collaborate with first line and second line colleagues to assess whether Third Party and BDR risks are appropriately identified, documented, managed, and escalated.
> Support targeted reviews and thematic analysis related to Third Party and BDR risk oversight.
> Engage with senior colleagues across the broader Firm, including first line of defense business units, support functions, and control partners, as appropriate.

> Understanding of Third Party and BDR related regulations and industry frameworks, especially relating to operational risk management

jobs.location: New York, New York, United States of America
jobs.description:
The Institutional Securities Group (ISG) has established the ISG Data Group (IDG) to provide a single point of accountability for the full spectrum of data-related commercial initiatives. These initiatives span the defensive aspects of data management, including data security and risk reduction, as well as opportunities to drive operational efficiency through improved data quality and enhanced revenue generation by leveraging data assets to deliver value-added services to clients.

The ISG Divisional Data Office (DDO), which sits within IDG, is responsible for the oversight, governance, and integrity of data used for senior management reporting, regulatory reporting, client reporting, and key internal controls. Using a risk-based prioritization framework, the team partners with business and control functions to identify critical data elements and implement enhancements to controls that ensure the quality, accuracy, and integrity of that data.

Position Description
Morgan Stanley is seeking a Vice President to join the ISG Divisional Data Office team. The successful candidate will partner with stakeholders across the business to assess and execute strategic data initiatives, evaluate front-office processes and their associated control frameworks, identify control gaps, and define remediation plans. The role will also oversee data issue management and support the development and presentation of metrics related to data governance, data quality, and policy implementation.

Primary Responsibilities
- Develop and maintain Data Management standards across ISG, focusing on data definitions, data ownership, data quality rules, control frameworks, and industry best practices in data governance and management.

- Build subject matter expertise in key data governance processes, controls, and regulatory expectations.

- Understand and apply Data Policy requirements to ensure appropriate cataloging and documentation of data initiatives and projects.

- Analyze relationships between data entities and perform basic data modeling to support data cataloging and governance activities.

- Evaluate the control environment, support control documentation efforts, and map controls to critical data elements.

- Assess data quality requirements, identify control gaps, and challenge stakeholders on fitness-for-purpose standards where appropriate.

- Collaborate with business, technology, and control partners to execute data initiatives and establish consistent data definitions and standards.

- Assess and prioritize data issues based on risk, perform root cause analysis, conduct thematic reviews, and drive remediation or risk-acceptance decisions for significant data issues.

- Prepare and present updates, metrics, and reporting on data policy implementation, data issue management, governance initiatives, and escalation items to senior management and Data Governance Committees.

- Track project milestones and deliverables, provide status updates to senior management, and proactively identify risks, dependencies, and potential impacts to timelines.

- 7+ years of experience within the financial services industry.

- Strong understanding of financial products, asset classes, and risk measures.

- Knowledge of the trade lifecycle and front-to-back (F2B) data lineage and data flows.

- Experience in a Data Management, Data Governance, or Data Quality role, with a focus on data definitions, ownership, quality controls, and governance frameworks.

- Solid understanding of Data Governance and Data Management principles and best practices.

- Strong analytical and data investigation skills, with the ability to identify trends, anomalies, inconsistencies, and control weaknesses.

- Demonstrated risk and control mindset with the ability to challenge assumptions and enhance processes.

- Ability to synthesize and present complex information in a clear and meaningful manner.

- Strong collaboration skills, with the ability to partner effectively across business, technology, and control functions.

- Highly motivated, delivery-focused, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
